title: Inverse image induced by a continuous left-exact site functor and its tensor structure
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] whose objects and morphisms are small in one universe; take sheaves of sets and abelian groups in a larger universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose $\mathcal C$ has finite limits and $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserves them and sends coverings to coverings. Then left Kan extension along $u^{op}$ followed by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] exists and gives a functor $L:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ left adjoint to $G\mapsto G\circ u^{op}$. The functor $L$ preserves finite limits and all colimits, so this adjunction is a geometric morphism $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. On abelian sheaves the same construction is additive and exact. With sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], there are canonical isomorphisms $L(F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G)\cong LF\otimes_{\mathbf Z}LG$ and $L\underline{\mathbf Z}\cong\underline{\mathbf Z}$, giving a strong symmetric monoidal structure. Under these tensor structures, the inverse-image composition and identity isomorphisms compatible with the adjunctions are monoidal natural isomorphisms, for composable functors satisfying the same hypotheses.

proof.text: The finite-limit hypothesis gives the covering fibre-product comparisons in the definition of continuity, and cover preservation gives its other clause. The continuous-pushforward node therefore shows that precomposition R sends sheaves to sheaves. Apply the adjunction node in sets and in abelian groups: L is precisely sheafification of the left Kan extension along u^op and L is left adjoint to R. Smallness makes each comma category small, so its colimit exists in the stipulated larger universe.

The presheaf-pullback node (2) applies because C has finite limits and u preserves them: every comma category I_W^op is filtered and the set-valued Kan extension preserves finite limits. Inclusion of sheaves into presheaves preserves limits by the sectionwise-limits node, and sheafification preserves finite limits by the sheafification node. Their composite L therefore preserves finite limits. The left-adjoint-colimits node applied to the preceding adjunction gives all colimits. Thus the adjunction is a geometric morphism in the stated direction.

The preceding continuity and set-valued finite-limit preservation make u a morphism of sites, so the abelian-exactness node applies without adding a hypothesis: the abelian L is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits, hence short exact sequences. Its adjunction from step 1 also gives all colimits. The underlying-sheaf node identifies the underlying sets of abelian L with set-valued L. Its group operations are the images of the original operations: the adjunction unit is an abelian homomorphism, and uniqueness of adjuncts determines addition and zero after the product comparisons of step 2.

Write V for underlying sheaves of sets. A map from F tensor_Z G to an abelian sheaf H is uniquely a natural sectionwise Z-bilinear map VF times VG to VH: first use the ordinary sectionwise tensor universal property and then the sheafification adjunction. For any abelian sheaf H on D, set-valued adjunction and the product comparison give bijections Bilin(F,G,RH) = Bilin(LF,LG,H). Explicitly, b on the left has adjunct beta = epsilon_VH composed with Lb composed with the inverse of L(VF times VG) -> VLF times VLG; the inverse sends beta to Rbeta composed with (eta_VF,eta_VG). Naturality and the triangle identities make these inverse. Bilinearity is preserved in both directions: transpose the equation b(a+a_prime,c)=b(a,c)+b(a_prime,c) on VF times VF times VG, using preservation of this triple product and addition from step 3; transpose the equation in the second variable on VF times VG times VG. The zero equations transpose using the terminal object, and integer linearity follows from additivity. Thus Hom(L(F tensor_Z G),H) = Bilin(F,G,RH) = Bilin(LF,LG,H) = Hom(LF tensor_Z LG,H), naturally in H. Applying these bijections to identity maps gives mutually inverse tensor comparisons. The forward comparison is adjoint to (s,t) -> eta_F(s) tensor eta_G(t), fixing its normalization and naturality.

proof.text: Define underline{Z} as sheafification of the constant presheaf Z. A map underline{Z} -> H is uniquely a compatible family h_U in H(U), the image of 1; equivalently it is a map from the terminal sheaf to VH. The sheafification adjunction, the abelian adjunction, the set adjunction and L(*) = * therefore give Hom(L underline{Z}_C,H) = Hom(underline{Z}_C,RH) = Hom(*_C,RVH) = Hom(*_D,VH) = Hom(underline{Z}_D,H). Identity maps give inverse unit comparisons. The comparison sends the pullback of 1 to 1 and, by additivity, the pullback of n to n for every integer n.

proof.text: The composition node supplies the adjunction-compatible inverse-image comparison for two composable site functors (with its labels relabelled to our orientation); its unit compatibility sends the generator eta_composite(s) to eta_second(eta_first(s)). The identity comparison sends eta_identity(s) to s by the triangle identity. To check the monoidal diagrams, take adjuncts and precompose with the universal bilinear map F times G -> F tensor_Z G: both composition routes send (s,t) to eta_second(eta_first(s)) tensor eta_second(eta_first(t)), and both identity routes send (s,t) to s tensor t. The unit routes send 1 to 1. These checks determine the maps because of the Hom/Bilin bijections of step 4 and the unit bijections of step 5; they do not assume that pullback sheaves are evaluated by precomposition. For associativity, after the same adjunction and universal-map reductions both routes send (s,t,r) to (eta(s) tensor eta(t)) tensor eta(r), identified with eta(s) tensor (eta(t) tensor eta(r)) by associativity. For symmetry both send (s,t) to eta(t) tensor eta(s). For the left and right unit diagrams both send (n,s) or (s,n) to n eta(s). The elementary identities for ordinary tensors descend through sheafification by its uniqueness property. Consequently the tensor and unit comparisons define a strong symmetric monoidal functor, and the composition and identity comparisons are monoidal.
